$meta.readThisFirst: Three sibling filter atoms — Filter_dropdown, Filter_Toggle, Filter_checkbox — share ONE container spec and ONE per-state colour model. RULED by Singh 2026-09-04: the three types are FINAL — follow the design exactly. The DROPDOWN is the default filter (multi-value; shows its selected value inline as ' : [Value]'). TOGGLE and CHECKBOX are SPECIAL-CASE filters, used ONLY when the value is a single binary with active/inactive states — the control's own on/off (checked/unchecked) IS the value. The container's State (Default/Active/Hover) marks whether the filter is applied or hovered and is a SEPARATE concern from the control's value. See usageGuidance and criticalFinding (resolved).

purpose: A row of compact, single-line filter controls that sit in a table's Search & Filters bar and let someone narrow the rows below. Each atom names ONE filter and carries the control appropriate to that filter's value type: a dropdown (pick one of many), a toggle (on/off), or a checkbox (include/exclude). They do not filter on their own — the row's Apply button commits them; Reset clears them.

stateColourModel.note: The whole point of the component. Verified per-state on the Filter_dropdown symbols; the identical model is confirmed on Filter_Toggle and Filter_checkbox Active symbols. bg = fill; border = 1px stroke.

Active.meaning: A value IS applied. The filter is engaged.

Hover.meaning: Pointer-over an applied filter. Same blue-tint fill as Active but a GREY border — this is the only visual difference from Active.

stateColourModel.summaryTable: Default = white bg + grey border · Active = blue-tint bg + blue border · Hover = blue-tint bg + grey border. Fill is the same for Active and Hover; the BORDER carries the difference.

controls.note: Each atom embeds one already-published control component. Per Singh's ruling (usageGuidance): toggle/checkbox are binary filters — the control's own active/inactive IS the value, and the container's State is a separate applied/hover cue.

colour.note: Measured on Default; the Active symbol did not re-bind an icon colour — treat as inherited.

boxRadius.note: Square corners — the box is NOT rounded, unlike the atom container (4px).

usageGuidance.rule: The three filter types are intentional and FINAL — follow the design exactly; do not add, drop or re-style states.

whenToUseEach.dropdown: The DEFAULT filter. Use for a normal filter that picks one value out of many; it shows the chosen value inline as ' : [Value]'.
whenToUseEach.toggle: SPECIAL CASE. Use ONLY when the filter's value is a single binary — an active / inactive (on / off) choice. The toggle's own on/off is the value.
whenToUseEach.checkbox: SPECIAL CASE. Use ONLY when the filter's value is a single binary — include / exclude (checked / unchecked). The checkbox's own state is the value.

usageGuidance.pickBy: Value type decides the control: many possible values → dropdown (default); one binary value → toggle or checkbox.

criticalFinding.title: Toggle/checkbox filters are binary (single-value) filters — RESOLVED, not a defect.
criticalFinding.measured: On the published Active (Value=Yes) symbols the toggle binds action/toggle/bg-default (the off track, 26938:65220) and the checkbox binds field/bg-default + border/medium with no check fill (26938:65447); the container carries the blue applied-cue. Flagged as a possible defect on 2026-09-04.
criticalFinding.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-09-04 (Singh): the three types are intentional — follow exactly. Dropdown is the DEFAULT (multi-value) filter; Toggle and Checkbox are SPECIAL-CASE filters used ONLY when the value is a single binary with active/inactive (on/off, checked/unchecked) states — the control's own state IS the value. The container's State (Default/Active/Hover) and the control's value are SEPARATE concerns. Not a defect; do not redesign the control. See usageGuidance.

behaviour.note: Singh's standing rule: every component carries its behaviour, not just its look.

table.do: Open a dropdown filter and pick a value
table.happens: Atom moves to Active: blue fill + blue border, and the label becomes 'Filter_Name : [Value]'. The table does NOT change yet.

table.do: Turn on a toggle filter / tick a checkbox filter
table.happens: The control's own active/inactive IS the value (these are binary filters per usageGuidance). The container also moves to Active (blue fill + blue border) to mark it applied. The table does NOT change yet.
Blue fill stays; border goes grey (Hover state).
Commits every engaged filter to the table below. Nothing filters until this is pressed.
Clears all filters back to Default (no value).

behaviour.applyResetOwnership: Apply and Reset are Button components living in the Search & Filters row, not part of the filter atom. The atom only holds its own value; the row commits it.

stateChangeNote: Moving between Default / Active / Hover swaps only the bg + border tokens (and, for the dropdown alone, appends the value text). Geometry, control and label are unchanged. This is a clean token-swap component EXCEPT that the dropdown also changes width when a value is shown (106 → 158).

openQuestions.question: On toggle and checkbox filters, should the control reflect the applied value, or is the container's blue styling the only cue?
openQuestions.status: RESOLVED 2026-09-04 (Singh): the three types are final — follow exactly. Dropdown is the default multi-value filter; toggle/checkbox are special-case binary filters (single value, active/inactive) whose own control state IS the value. See usageGuidance + criticalFinding.

openQuestions.question: Is there a Hover state for a filter with NO value applied ((Hover, No))? Only (Hover, Yes) is published. A no-value filter presumably still needs hover feedback.
The three atoms are named Filter_dropdown / Filter_Toggle / Filter_checkbox with placeholder 'Filter_Name'. What real filter names/value types map to each in the Agency product?
openQuestions.gate: BA / product content — not a design-system decision.
